newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Socgen-Crosby sees H-share profits plunging in '96.
newsitem.headline: Socgen-Crosby sees H-share profits plunging in '96.

text.p: Socgen-Crosby Securities (HK) Ltd has forecast net profits of H-share companies will drop by an average of 35.2 percent in calendar 1996.
H-share companies are listed in Hong Kong but backed by Chinese parents or well-connected to the mainland.
Earnings per share would plunge by an average of 38.2 percent in 1996 against a drop of 18.8 percent a year earlier, Socgen-Crosby said in a January 1997 research report.

Dividend yield was estimated at 2.6 percent and the average price-earnings ratio was 17.8 times on projected 1996 earnings when the H-share index was at 1,034.90, Socgen-Crosby investment analyst Xue Lan said.
The H-share index closed Wednesday at 971.35, down 13.97 points.

"I think most of the H-share companies are industrial stocks so they are affected by (China's) tight credit policy and they do not have the flexibility to really tap into other areas which may have offered better growth," Xue told reporters.
"So we are expecting very, very bad results for 1996. But for 1997, overall the H-share sector will perform better," she added.
The brokerage urged caution in view of an already demanding H-share market price-earnings ratio of about 18 times on both 1996 and 1997 earnings following price rises since December.
But it recommended Anhui Expressway Co Ltd, Guangdong Kelon Electrical Holdings Co Ltd, Dongfang Electrical Machinery Co Ltd, Qingling Motor Co Ltd and Zhenhai Refining & Chemical Co Ltd.
